title: The 7 Most Islamophobic Things That Republicans Have Said Just This Year Alone
author: Team Zeteo
content:
On Monday, two teenage suspects opened fire in San Diego's biggest mosque,
[killing three people](https://www.cnn.com/2026/05/18/us/live-news/san-diego-
islamic-center-shooting). The attack is only the latest incident in a [rising
tide of Islamophobia](https://www.cair.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/02/CAIR-2025-Annual-
Report.pdf?utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email) that's swept the U.S. - from
the [stabbing to death of a 6-year-old
boy](https://www.cnn.com/2023/10/16/us/chicago-muslim-boy-stabbing-
investigation) after Oct. 7 to an [assault on Representative Ilhan
Omar](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/rep-ilhan-omar-attack-sprayed-at-town-
hall/) in January.

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

Republican leaders have been fueling the fire with unfailingly bigoted,
inflammatory language against Muslims and their faith. GOP Twitter has raged
against "[Jihadi Mamdani](https://x.com/RepFine/status/2052389206064787741)"
and ridiculously claimed the country is backsliding into a so-called "[United
Caliphate of
America](https://x.com/CoachForGov/status/2000237132313747610?s=20)." In a
moment when houses of worship are no longer sanctuaries, some of the highest
elected officials in the U.S. are working tirelessly to make sure Muslims feel
unsafe wherever they turn.
